## Overview

**Time:** ~20 minutes  
**Goal:** Create a GitHub account, make a private repository, and share it
with your instructor. You will use this repository to save and submit your
work throughout the semester.

You do **not** need RStudio for this exercise — everything is done in a
web browser at [https://github.com](https://github.com).

---

## Step 1 — Create a GitHub Account

1. Go to **[https://github.com](https://github.com)** and click **Sign up**
2. Choose a **username**. Tips:
   - Use something professional — this account is visible to future employers
     and collaborators
   - Lowercase letters and hyphens are best (e.g., `jane-smith`)
   - Avoid random numbers if possible
3. Use your **university email address** — this makes you eligible for free
   GitHub Education benefits
4. Complete the verification steps and confirm your email

> ✅ **Checkpoint:** You can log in and view your profile page at
> `https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME`

---

## Step 2 — Create a New Private Repository

1. Click the **+** icon in the top-right corner → **New repository**
2. Fill in the form:
   - **Repository name:** `MBE713-YourLastName`
     (e.g., `MBE713-Smith`)
   - **Description:** `MBE 713 Population Dynamics — student work`
   - **Visibility:** Select **Private** ← *this is important!*
   - ☑ Check **Add a README file**
3. Click **Create repository**

> ✅ **Checkpoint:** You should see your new repository page with a single
> `README.md` file.

---

## Step 3 — Edit Your README

A README is the front page of your repository. Let's add your information.

1. Click on `README.md` in your repository
2. Click the **pencil icon** (✏️) on the right to edit the file
3. Replace all the existing text with the following, filling in your own
   information:

```
# MBE 713 — Population Dynamics

**Student:** Your Full Name  
**Program:** Your Program  
**GitHub username:** @your-username  

## About this repository
This repository contains my coursework for MBE 713, Population Dynamics,
taught by Dr. Babcock at the University of Miami.
```

4. Scroll down to **Commit changes**
5. In the commit message box, write: `Add student info to README`
6. Leave **Commit directly to the main branch** selected
7. Click **Commit changes**

> ✅ **Checkpoint:** Your README now displays your name and program on the
> repository front page.

**Question:** What is a *commit*? Write a one-sentence definition in your
own words.

> *Your answer here:*

---

## Step 4 — Share Your Repository with the Instructor

Your repository is private, so the instructor cannot see it yet.
You need to add them as a **collaborator**.

1. In your repository, click **Settings** (in the top menu bar)
2. In the left sidebar, click **Collaborators**
3. Click **Add people**
4. Search for the instructor's GitHub username: **`ebabcock`**
5. Select the correct account and click **Add ebabcock to this repository**

> ✅ **Checkpoint:** You should see `ebabcock` listed as a collaborator
> with "Pending" status until the invitation is accepted.

---

## Step 5 — Submit

Submit the following in the course portal (or by email to your instructor):

- Your **GitHub username**
- The **full URL of your repository**
  (e.g., `https://github.com/jsmith/MBE713-Smith`)

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Solution |
|---|---|
| Can't find the **Settings** tab | You may be inside a file view. Click the repository name at the very top to return to the main repository page. |
| **Collaborators** option is missing from Settings | Make sure the repository is yours — you can only manage collaborators on repositories you own. |
| Can't find `ebabcock` when searching | Double-check the spelling. Confirm the account exists at `https://github.com/ebabcock`. |
| Accidentally made the repository **Public** | Go to Settings → scroll to the **Danger Zone** at the bottom → **Change repository visibility** → Private. |
| Forgot your password | Use **Forgot password** on the login page — this is why using your university email matters. |

## Why Are We Doing This?

| GitHub Concept | What You Just Did |
|---|---|
| **Repository** | Created a project folder tracked by Git |
| **README** | Added a human-readable description of the project |
| **Commit** | Saved a change with a descriptive message |
| **Private repository** | Kept your work visible only to people you choose |
| **Collaborator** | Granted another user read/write access to your private repo |

You will use this same repository throughout the semester to save and
submit your R scripts, plots, and analysis outputs. Every commit you make
builds a timestamped record of your work — like a lab notebook that never
gets lost.
